Join lists of annotation results to library match output

Source: R/wrapper_join_annotation_results.R
join_annotation_results.Rd

Combine direct library match results (MS1/MS2) with downstream annotation results (adduct/isotope/MS2 fragment/NL) onto the feature table.

Tier naming convention:

  • 1a — adduct match (Phase 1, within library group)

  • 1b — isotope (Phase 1, within library group)

  • 1c — MS2 fragment match (Phase 1: feature already in a Phase 1 library group)

  • 1d — neutral loss (Phase 1, pairwise within group)

  • 1a_exp / 1b_exp / 1c_exp / 1d_exp — Phase 2 expansions (feature NOT assigned in Phase 1; derived from a Phase 1 confirmed M)

  • 2 — unexplained (in group, no rule fires)

Tiers are mutually exclusive — one tier per feature, highest priority wins: 1a > 1b > 1c > 1d > 2 > 1a_exp > 1b_exp > 1c_exp > 1d_exp. Tier2 (Unexplained) is a Phase 1 assignment and therefore outranks all Phase 2 expansions.

The annotation_phase column takes exactly two values: "Phase1" (any Tier 1a/1b/1c/1d or Tier 2 assignment) and "Phase2" (any _exp tier). Sub-labels such as Phase1_MS2frag or Phase2_IsoExpansion are not used; reference_tier already encodes the specific evidence type.

Usage

join_annotation_results(
  FT,
  direct_lib_list,
  lib_anno_list = NULL,
  target_match_list = NULL,
  isf_result = NULL,
  include_phase2 = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

FT

Required data.frame. Feature table.

direct_lib_list

Required list.

lib_anno_list

Optional list/data.frame. Output of annotate().

target_match_list

Optional list/data.frame. Target list annotations.

isf_result

Optional data.frame. Output of annotateISF() / run_isf_annotation(). Adds Tier 1c / 1c_exp columns and resolves reference_tier by priority.

include_phase2

Logical. If FALSE, Phase 2 expansion rows (Tier1a_exp, Tier1b_exp, Tier1d_exp) from lib_anno_list are excluded from the output. Default TRUE.

verbose

Logical. If FALSE, suppresses all progress messages. Default TRUE.
